[b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] has an incredible amount of potential, but I struggle to understand how such an interesting universe can feel so average in its execution. I first tried it in 2020 and disliked almost everything, from the story to the gameplay. Returning several years later, I can recognise the improvements, but many fundamental problems remain. Night City is beautiful, its architecture and visual design are impressive, and the universe has enormous potential. Unfortunately, a beautiful city filled with NPCs does not automatically become a living world.

One of my biggest problems is how superficial the world feels. Too many NPCs exist simply to fill the streets. Most stand around doing practically nothing, staring into the distance or repeating basic animations. You occasionally see characters talking, but these interactions rarely develop into anything meaningful. I am not asking for every NPC to have a complex routine or storyline. I mean basic everyday life: people interacting, recognising familiar faces, following routines and reacting naturally. Night City should feel like a place that exists independently of the player. Instead, it feels like a backdrop. Fewer NPCs with meaningful interactions would have been better than streets full of characters that barely do anything.

Other open-world games handle this better. The Witcher 3 makes Geralt feel connected to the world, with people recognising him as a mutant. Bethesda games also use conversations and NPC reactions to acknowledge the player's presence and actions. In Skyrim, even a bard singing about your achievements makes your progress feel relevant. Cyberpunk rarely creates that connection. Mission characters may know V is a mercenary, but the rest of the world barely acknowledges who you are or what you have accomplished. You experience Night City without feeling that you belong there. I had a similar feeling in Hogwarts Legacy: you visit an interesting universe without becoming properly integrated into it.

The narrative has similar problems. The three life paths suggest that your background will matter, but they eventually converge into practically the same direction. The game also does very little to establish who V actually is, offering little personal history about their family or circumstances. The relationship with Jackie Welles is another missed opportunity. We are expected to care about a friendship that has already developed before we get to experience most of it. Skipping that important period makes the emotional connection harder to establish and the experience feel even shorter. For a game with this much potential, the narrative feels shallow, with little suspense or weight.

Exploration and side content contribute to this problem. Missions and activities are scattered across the map, sometimes requiring ridiculous distances between objectives without natural progression through the districts. Unlike GTA, where progression can gradually open up areas, Cyberpunk throws activities everywhere from the beginning. I barely found a reason to use the metro, and once I discovered fast travel points, driving became increasingly unnecessary. Many activities feel like they exist simply to fill the map. Exploration should offer more than another weapon or piece of equipment. A world this interesting should reward curiosity with meaningful discoveries.

The police and general AI systems are another major disappointment. The police feel incredibly weak. NPCs can attack the player without meaningful intervention, and I rarely saw convincing pursuits involving other NPCs. Gang-controlled areas also fail to communicate the danger they are supposed to represent. Meanwhile, ordinary NPCs panic over the smallest contact. Some run directly in front of your vehicle or refuse to move when you are leaving an alley. In some situations, NPCs run into my car and the police somehow decide that I am the problem. At three wanted stars or more, police officers also start appearing directly in your field of vision. This is not how a convincing police system should behave.

Vehicle pursuits are particularly bad. They are among the weakest action sequences I have experienced in an open-world game. Vehicles feel strangely slow, and you cannot properly ram enemy cars or force them off course. Enemy vehicles behave like indestructible objects following predetermined routes. It becomes even more frustrating when the narrative protects certain characters or vehicles because they must survive until a specific point. The game creates the illusion of a dynamic chase while restricting what the player can actually do. If you cannot meaningfully influence the encounter, why create that illusion?

Adam Smasher is another example of the gap between presentation and execution. He is presented as an absolute monster, a massive cybernetic killing machine who should feel intimidating. After seeing his portrayal in Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, I expected something much more memorable. Instead, the boss fight was embarrassing. Using a shotgun and landing headshots made the encounter surprisingly easy. He fired missiles and used his other weapons, but I could withstand everything he threw at me. For a character with this much importance, the actual confrontation is incredibly underwhelming.

Johnny Silverhand also feels like a character whose potential was not properly developed. His identity as a musician, his history with Samurai and his role in the destruction of Arasaka Tower could have been explored much better. The game never makes his music feel as memorable as it should. I never found a track that made me interested in Samurai or gave Johnny's musical identity the impact the story expects. *I Really Want to Stay at Your House* gained a much stronger emotional association through Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, especially with David and Lucy. The anime gave the song a memorable context that the game never managed to establish. It is a shame, because Johnny could have had a much stronger musical identity.

Then there are the technical problems. Despite years of updates, I still encountered a ridiculous number of bugs. Some character storyline finales and expansion-related quests became completely stuck, preventing progression. I sometimes had to load an earlier save. It is disappointing that progression blockers still exist, with some situations apparently requiring mods to work around them even in a vanilla playthrough. I also encountered NPCs walking through walls, vehicles spawning on top of each other and creating pile-ups, collisions and flying cars. In two locations, my character suddenly accelerated backwards, as if a time-rewind ability had activated, before getting attached to a random wall like Spider-Man. Character models sometimes rendered without hands, and objects disappeared during cutscenes. I even have video clips of some incidents. I understand that bugs can be inconsistent between players, but these were part of my experience.

I can recognise the improvements since launch and appreciate what Cyberpunk 2077 does well. Night City is visually impressive, and its universe has enormous potential. That is precisely what makes the experience so frustrating. The game constantly gives you glimpses of something greater without delivering on it. A large open world is not automatically immersive, a huge number of NPCs does not create a living city, and a collection of activities does not make exploration meaningful. The narrative, world simulation, AI, police systems and major action sequences all feel underdeveloped. Cyberpunk 2077 is an average experience built around an extraordinary universe. I wanted to experience Night City as a living world, not simply walk through a beautiful backdrop. Unfortunately, that is exactly how much of the experience felt to me.

I think it's both easy and difficult to describe just how good of a game Cyberpunk 2077 turned out to be from the way I experienced it. In one sentence, Cyberpunk 2077 is probably one of the most well-made, wholeheartedly complete games that exists out there. The entire world of Cyberpunk basically lived by its code of making a name for yourself that it itself spawned a majorly successful anime, collaborations, comics and books, a whole new fandom out of it. Just the CD Projekt effect maybe. 

Else, Cyberpunk 2077 certainly has some flaws that to others may have been the arrow to the knee for them, but I'm going to be describing how I felt. And in spite of the minor flaws it had, as a whole, I felt very, VERY content with it all. 

I spent the past year and a bit playing this game, on and off, taking breaks that were months long before picking it up again, and every time I did, I got right back into the groove of completely absorbing myself into the world of Night City like I never left. Some games when I've played after a certain time away from it, I end up struggling to reconnect. But with Cyberpunk, it never felt like that at all. 

Every character actually had depth. I sympathised with more than one character and wanted to learn of their back stories more than ever. Learning characters back stories? Who would've thought. The side gigs - sure, some of them got repetitive - but they at least were different in that each gig occasionally had motives. They had clues, evidence of something else going on, and at some point Cyberpunk 2077 the action RPG turned into a mystery thriller game. The combat is extremely versatile. I mostly played a Netrunner build for my V with quickhacks and non-confrontational attacks, but when I restarted and decided to go for a mostly Mercenary frontal assault V, it was just as smooth of a transition to be a ruthless killer slicing enemies with katanas and shooting everybody down with the spray of your machine gun. 

I finished the whole game, completed all gigs, got all tarots, played the DLC with all endings through and through, and I can say without a doubt that I'll be remembering Cyberpunk 2077 for a long time. In fact, I know that once I finish this review to go to uninstall this game, I'm actually going to miss it. I intend to keep it as one of my most favourite games of all time for the kind of impact it has on my experience as a gamer towards video games, and if anything, I hope that when people pick this game up or wonder if this game was the right choice to start playing, they haven't seen anything yet.

I mostly enjoyed the hacking-oriented skills combined with gunplay. For those who like to cater their perks to playstyle, there is plenty to customize to your hearts content.

Great game been really enjoying it. If you have specs similar to mine and can't figure out how to run it with good picture with minimum stutters use this setup for 1080p. 

Open Nvidia control panel global settings in Manage 3D Settings, DSR=On 2.25x DL Sharpness=33/default, Low Latency=Ultra, Threaded Optimization=On 
Next go to add program section with the control panel right next to global settings add the exe file for Cyberpunk2077 set MaxFrameRate=60 and enable Vsync=Fast also have Textures=Quality
Finally launch the game turn off Vsync and MaxFrameRate in game, turn on DLSS to Quality with sharpness=40
Set crowd population to low everything else medium to high. ray tracing off.
Hope these settings help you enjoy it like i have been! Final note make sure your framerate within windows setting is set to max mine is 180hz but i use control panel as a limiter because of my cpu bottleneck.

Cyberpunk 2077 dares to ask: what if Dave Mustaine was in your head, and - what if he looked like the guy from The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

This game and the studio behind it are preceded by their reputation. Cyberpunk 2077 is a messy game. It had a trouble development, a troubled launch and even a troubled post-launch update and expansion cycle. But, here I am, leaving a positive review after well over a hundred hours with it. So, what's the deal?

Well, Cyberpunk 2077 has managed to be both great and terrible, in equal measure, at different points of its life. It delivers a fantastic rendition of Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk...visually. Mechanically, this game bears the scars of its many patch-surgeries, and 2.0's grand ambition to course-correct (which I think it does successfully for the most part). Narratively, this is more complicated, because so much of what this game was broadcasted to be - it was not, and to some extent is still not and never will be. The lifepaths are flavour, but not made equal: corpo gets the most choices, the most consequences and thematically feels the most coherent to me. Corpo V immerses you in the setting, puts you fairly high up on the food chain of this world, and shows you just how suddenly -unceremoniously- you can meet the ground. From there, V can embrace being a mercenary to satiate their lust for wealth, fame, revenge or 'salvation'. We'll get back to that in a bit, because just like CDPR's game structure, this review is going to meander in my word salad for a bit before the conclusion.

Cyberpunk 2077 starts off with a fantastic act 1, whose only fault at a glance seems that it's way too short. In truth, this is where the cracks form - selective freedom, selective choices of consequence and sometimes a glimpse of a game that is relegated to a montage rather than an experience. We tasted the fruit, then were fed sugary sand. 

Act 2: Sugary Sand. This is where the game begins enticing you with the promise of revelations, of payoffs, of consequences and of freedom. They are all half-truths. Get it? Half-truth...freedom...phantom libert--
In this act, the open world frees up a lot more. You will likely be past level 10 now, which means you get to pick more cyberware, hooray! You get to do more gigs than before, hooray, you get access to some really cool and actually good sidequests (especially because most of them are self-contained and can afford to house several outcomes as a result of being relatively short). You get to form bonds with the main roster of this game, and there won't be any 11th hour additions later which have no time to shine. This is where you also get the chance to jump into Phantom Liberty: this game's sugar, to this act's dunes of bloated content, with the oases of good writing hidden behind the map's ambiguous 'gig' markers (and sometimes none at all). The problem here is, the sheer amount of generic 'clear gangers and scavs' activities will sometimes hide actual interesting encounters, narratively and mechanically. But, to differentiate these and to know where to look for them, you will have to simply experience them all, or worse - consult a guide or fan-wiki to narrow your search. There is a silver lining here: by the time you do a third of these, the game's systems and builds will start to come online. Here, you will get to experience one of Cyberpunk 2077's sleeved-up aces: unique gameplay. Per playthrough, you will be incentivised to spec into one or two styles of play your V will excel at, and they will all feel good to play, be rewarding and feel unique from one another. Bonus points for the Edgerunners 2 update's dual-wielding, it fits right in and compliments this.
Act 2: 2.0 You Can (Not) Escape:
Phantom Liberty. Update 2.0. Honestly, what prompted me to return to this game, give it another chance after launch, and ultimately made me actually really like it. I will keep the details here to a minimum: Phantom Liberty capitalises on CP2077's capacity for cinematic spectacle, enriches and deepens its core gameplay, enhances the base game's conclusion and alleviates a lot of its 2nd act problems by offering a denser and sweeter chunk of storytelling and general loop. This is the game firing on all cylinders, without blowing all of its load before the encore. It does trudge along with some of the baggage of the core game's faults, but frankly they are an insignificant blemish at this point. This is the second peak of the game after Act 1, and its whispered promise for the ending, is another half-truth, but not one born out of messy development or unrealised vision, but rather the fulfillment of it. Play Phantom Liberty, it's really good.


Act 3: Salvation
Oh yeah, it's all coming together.
By this point, you know how the game works, your V's build is complete and the game trickles in its payoffs. Conclusions to quest chains, relationships, collectathons, the whole she-bang. The gang gets together for one last show, you have time to process it in the aftermath, and you get on to the ending. Every story needs one: this, however, happens to have a few. And...they are all actually excellent. Every ending ties into the main story, ties into the side quests, ties into every relationship you nourished or ran into the ground, and executes on the thematic motif that each different ending embodies. They all have a gameplay component - always different, always relevant to the story beat it pursues and always worthwhile. V dares death, come what may...

Cyberpunk 2077 realises a Night City that's a mish-mash between corporate America and the Berlin club scene, each cranked to eleven. The extremes - so abundant and brazen they skirt into banality. Its themes are evergreen, and beyond the bombastic spectacle; crude neon advertisements it greets you with, it carries with itself a somber and frightful maturity. This game has pacing issues, it has unrealised ambitions and it still creaks funny because of the bugs that haunt it. But, it delivers on some really solid writing, excellent worldbuilding and unique gameplay. Few games manage to make their spectacles as enticing as their moments of quiet, few manage to synergise them, but Cyberpunk 2077 is one of them. A messy, half-broken game, with a surprising amount of heart.

I purchased Cyberpunk 2077 in December of 2025 & have only just finished my first playthrough so I'm here to talk that along side Edgerunners Seasons 1 & 2.
Before watching Edgerunners 1 I purchased & started to play 2077 because it was 65% off at the time so I figured why not. I picked the Corpo start & made my way to Dex at which point I stopped & moved on to other games but never ended up going back. I tried a 2nd time after watching Edgerunners 1 with a bit of a sour taste as I was not a fan of season 1 due to the writing dessions but I'm not about to go into that as it wasn't the games fault. This time only making it to meet Jackie in Lizzies before putting it back down & not playing it again.
It took watching Edgerunners 2 to actually spark a want to play 2077 as I believe season 2 shined an interesting light on Night City. Picking 2077 back up this last week I eneded up putting about 40hours into the main mission & a handful of the side missions.
Female V, Corpo Start, focusing stats on Reflex & Technically Ability, once I gotten Air Dash. I put it into Intelligence & a bit more technically ability.

Playing the game it's very clear I have a major skill issue when it comes to driving as it felt like I couldn't keep control of most cars. Without a dedicated handbrake button every turn became an uncontrolable drift & therefore once I could I took up dashing & airdashing everywhere which was the right call to make as there was a plentful amount of roofs & highways/roads to jump between making my travels quicker than car would have been. 

The story so far as well has been great. The path I lead brought me to following Takemura & eventually trusting him after kidnapping Hanako & bringing her to Yorinobu in return for Arasaka to remove Johnny. Yes this does mean I choice to not let Johnny take over in the end but, I did still bring Johnny to Rogue for their Date & did 1 last gig with the Samurai as playing as V. It only felt right after he saved my life (twice) even tho I did have to 2nd thoughts after the 1st time I let him take control to meet with Rogue & had the wildest night. I did still promise to Flatline/Zero out Adam Smasher & I did & said my goodbyes the best I could but he didn't like me (us?) every much after taking the pill on Misty's roof. 

The game isn't without its flaws still. I would never have brought 2077 full price after seeing the release state but it has clearly been improved massively. In saying that here's a list of a some flaws still;
- Driving
See above
- Customisation options
For how many options you get for designing your face & body it doesn't feel like that was foillowed up with the clothing options available in-game. During downtime either waiting for messages to follow up on missions or not wanting to do other missions just yet I found myself checking out all the clothing shops & what was available didn't really feel like something I wanted to even consider as it was tacky or about 4 different recolours.
- Mini-map Task routing
The routing didn't seem to account for the fact I wasn't in a vichle & therefore didn't use any alleyways or sidwalks that I could see & was infact quicker than following the road. There was also a situation where the route just lead to a building & stopped, I went to the building even tho I knew I need to continue further to see what would happen & then it updated with the rest of the route.
- Not being able to pause/save.
Life happens & during some cutsenses you can't open the pause menu which means you can't save the game & come back it to. so while I have 48hours ingame my saves say I've only spent 35hours in it which leaves the rest of this time just having the game opened & 'paused' in the background on the Character menu.
- Looting
Sometimes (mostly with robots) it was impossible to loot them despite showing available loot as I couldn't find a way to access the drops.
- Random Menus appearing
Mostly against some walls a small menu will appear which usually meant there's option I can do but looking back over to find it was a very tiny small spot my cursor had to be on & it was an empty box with nothing there.

Despite these negatives and a few more I'm not going to mention cause they were minor ones I'd still recommend 2077 to most people as the story & gameplay is amazing. I do recommend having a beefy PC however, as with my specs running high-ultra settings would get me 60fps max & I wouldn't want to see this game anything visually lower just to keep the FPS as it is so beautful when you can run High-Ultra settings.

I'm about to start my 2nd playthrough as Male V, Streetkid start & given the chance Imma be raiding Arasaka as Johnny this time round🔥
